definition_zh: 坏的；糟糕的；变质的；严重的；有害的
definition_en: not good, or harmful and unpleasant
core_image: 一只苹果从里往外烂了一块
scene: 摊主把那筐水果挪到一边。The milk had gone bad in the heat.
sceneCN: 这里 bad 是「变质的」（第 2 个义项：食物腐坏不能吃）；句意是牛奶在高温下变质了。

pos.zh: 形容词：坏的；糟糕的；变质的；严重的

derivatives.zh: 由 bad 加 -ly 构成，义为「糟糕地；非常」
由 bad 加 -ness 构成，义为「坏；恶劣」
比较级形式，义为「更坏的」

senses.title: Not good
senses.definition: of poor quality or not satisfactory
senses.definitionCN: 质量差或不令人满意的
senses.example: It was a bad idea from the start.
senses.exampleCN: 这从一开始就是个坏主意。
senses.why: Bad is an old English word whose origin is uncertain, and its oldest recorded sense is simply 'inferior'.
senses.whyCN: bad 是古英语词，来源不明，最早记录的义项就是「较差」。

senses.title: Spoiled
senses.definition: no longer fresh or safe to eat
senses.definitionCN: 不再新鲜或不能安全食用
senses.example: The milk had gone bad in the heat.
senses.exampleCN: 牛奶在高温下变质了。
senses.why: Food that has lost its quality is bad in the same way as a bad plan, so the word covers rot as well as failure.
senses.whyCN: 食物失去品质，和糟糕的计划一样都是 bad，所以这个词既指腐坏也指失败。

senses.title: Serious or severe
senses.definition: serious or severe in degree
senses.definitionCN: 程度严重或剧烈
senses.example: She caught a bad cold last winter.
senses.exampleCN: 她去年冬天得了重感冒。
senses.why: Something bad can be not only wrong but large in force, which produced the sense of severity.
senses.whyCN: 坏的东西不仅可能不对，也可能来势很猛，这就产生了「严重」的义项。

senses.title: Harmful
senses.definition: damaging to health or success
senses.definitionCN: 对健康或成功有害的
senses.example: Too much sugar is bad for your teeth.
senses.exampleCN: 糖吃太多对牙齿有害。
senses.why: If a thing is not good for you, it works against you, so bad came to mark harm as well as poor quality.
senses.whyCN: 如果某物对你没好处，它就在跟你作对，所以 bad 也标记伤害，而不只是质量差。

intro.en: Bad is a native English word whose deeper origin is unknown.
intro.cn: bad 是英语本族词，更早的来源并不清楚。

items.en: bad already meant 'poor in quality'.
items.cn: bad 已经表示「质量差」。

items.en: It widened to moral faults.
items.cn: 它扩展到道德上的过失。

items.en: bad covered spoiled food and severe illness.
items.cn: bad 涵盖食物变质与病情严重。

items.en: It became one of the most general negative words.
items.cn: 它成为最通用的否定词之一。

items.en: Bad is also slang for 'very good'.
items.cn: 如今 bad 还有「非常棒」的俚语义。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one vowel; the near-meaning group gives shades of poor and harmful.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个元音；近义组是表示差与有害的词。

sensesIntro.en: Poor quality, rot, severity and harm are four shades of one negative judgment.

core.cn: 核心意象：一只从果核开始烂的苹果。

definition_en: in a poor way, severely, or very much
core_image: 一辆自行车歪倒在路边，轮子还在转
scene: 雨后的路面又滑又亮。He badly wanted to finish the race.
sceneCN: 这里 badly 是「非常」（第 3 个义项：表示程度很强烈）；句意是他非常想跑完这场比赛。

pos.zh: 副词：糟糕地；严重地；非常

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词，义为「坏的」，badly 由其加 -ly 构成
由 bad 加 -ness 构成，义为「坏；恶劣」

senses.title: In a poor way
senses.definition: in a way that is not good or skillful
senses.definitionCN: 以不好或不熟练的方式
senses.example: The team played badly in the second half.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队下半场打得很糟。
senses.why: Badly is bad plus -ly, and its first job is to describe an action done without skill or success.
senses.whyCN: badly 是 bad 加 -ly，最初用于描述缺乏技巧或没有成功的动作。

senses.title: Severely
senses.definition: to a serious or severe degree
senses.definitionCN: 达到严重或剧烈的程度
senses.example: He was badly hurt in the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 他在那次摔倒中受了重伤。
senses.why: A bad injury is a severe one, so the adverb came to mean severely when it describes damage.
senses.whyCN: bad injury 是严重的伤，所以副词在描述损害时就表示「严重地」。

senses.title: Very much
senses.definition: very much or strongly
senses.definitionCN: 程度很深或很强烈
senses.example: He badly wanted to finish the race.
senses.exampleCN: 他非常想跑完这场比赛。
senses.why: Wanting something in a bad way is wanting it intensely, which is how badly became an intensifier.
senses.whyCN: 以很糟的状态想要某物，就是极想要，badly 由此变成了程度副词。

intro.en: Badly is the adverb built on bad.
intro.cn: badly 是建在 bad 上的副词。

items.en: bad meant 'poor in quality'.
items.cn: bad 意为「质量差」。

items.en: bad widened to moral and physical faults.
items.cn: bad 扩展到道德与身体缺陷。

items.en: badly meant 'in a poor way'.
items.cn: badly 意为「以糟糕的方式」。

items.en: It also meant severely and very much.
items.cn: 它也表示「严重地」与「非常」。

items.en: Badly need is a common phrase.
items.cn: badly need 是常见搭配。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -ly ending; the near-meaning group gives degrees of poor and severe.
note.cn: 形近组都以 -ly 结尾；近义组是表示差与严重的词。

entries.definition: in a plain and direct way

normalIntro.en: Badly measures poor skill, severe damage or strong desire.
normalIntro.cn: badly 衡量的是差劲的手艺、严重的损害或强烈的愿望。

normal.en: The comparative is worse, like the adjective.
normal.cn: 比较级与形容词一样是 worse。

normal.en: Badly hurt and badly damaged are very common pairs.
normal.cn: badly hurt 与 badly damaged 是常见搭配。

normal.en: Want something badly means want it very much.

normal.en: Badly does not mean 'in a bad mood'.
normal.cn: badly 并不表示「心情不好」。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: BAD-ly.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节。

root: 由 bad 加 -ly 构成；bad 源自古英语，词源不明；副词由「以糟糕方式」引申出「严重地」与「非常」。

sensesIntro.en: Poor performance, severe damage and intense desire are one adverb in three strengths.
sensesIntro.cn: 做得糟、伤得重与想得厉害，是同一个副词的三档强度。

core.cn: 核心意象：一辆歪倒在路边的自行车。

intro.cn: 后缀 -ly 把 bad 变成副词，比较级仍然是 worse。

definition_en: a soft container for carrying things, or to put something into one
core_image: 一只布袋鼓鼓地挂在椅背上
scene: 门口堆着刚买的东西。She packed the fruit into a paper bag.
sceneCN: 这里 bag 是「袋子」（第 1 个义项：用软材料做的容器）；句意是她把水果装进了一个纸袋。

derivatives.zh: 由 bag 加 -ful 构成，义为「一袋之量」
由 bag 与 -age 构成，义为「行李」
由 bag 加 -y 构成，义为「宽松的」

senses.title: A soft container
senses.definition: a container made of paper, cloth or plastic, open at the top
senses.definitionCN: 用纸、布或塑料制成、顶部开口的容器
senses.example: She packed the fruit into a paper bag.
senses.exampleCN: 她把水果装进了一个纸袋。
senses.why: Bag probably comes from Old Norse baggi, a pack or bundle, so the word began with the idea of a load carried together.
senses.whyCN: bag 可能来自古诺斯语 baggi「包裹、一捆」，所以这个词起初就有「把东西收在一起背着」的意思。

senses.title: A piece of luggage
senses.definition: a bag used for travel or for carrying personal things
senses.definitionCN: 旅行或随身携带物品用的包
senses.example: He left his bag at the hotel.
senses.exampleCN: 他把包落在了旅馆。
senses.why: A travel bag is simply the container sense narrowed to the things a person carries on a journey.
senses.whyCN: 旅行包只是把「容器」义缩小到旅途中随身携带的东西。

senses.title: To take or claim
senses.definition: to get or claim something, often before others
senses.definitionCN: 常指抢在别人之前拿到或占有
senses.example: They bagged the best seats by arriving early.
senses.exampleCN: 他们早到占到了最好的座位。
senses.why: Putting something into your bag is a concrete way of claiming it, which produced the informal verb sense.
senses.whyCN: 把东西装进自己的袋子，是占有它的具体做法，由此产生了口语里的动词义。

intro.en: Bag probably came from the Norse word for a pack.
intro.cn: bag 很可能来自诺斯语中表示「包裹」的词。

items.en: baggi meant 'a pack or bundle'.
items.cn: baggi 意为「包裹、一捆」。

items.en: bagge meant 'a sack'.
items.cn: bagge 意为「袋子」。

items.en: bag covered travel and shopping containers.
items.cn: bag 涵盖旅行与购物用的容器。

items.en: The verb bag meant 'to put into a bag'.
items.cn: 动词 bag 意为「装进袋子」。

items.en: Bag also means to claim something first.
items.cn: 如今 bag 也指抢先占得某物。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one vowel; the near-meaning group gives other containers.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个元音；近义组是其他容器。

normalIntro.en: A bag is a soft mouth that holds whatever you put in.
normalIntro.cn: bag 是一张柔软的嘴，装进什么就含住什么。

normal.en: The plural is bags, and the verb past is bagged.
normal.cn: 复数是 bags，动词过去式是 bagged。

normal.en: Pack a bag means prepare for a trip.
normal.cn: pack a bag 意为收拾行李准备出行。

normal.en: Bag a seat is informal for claiming a seat.
normal.cn: bag a seat 是「占座」的口语说法。

normal.en: Baggage is the uncountable word for all the bags.
normal.cn: baggage 是不可数的「行李」总称。

normal.en: The vowel is short: bag, not baag.
normal.cn: 元音是短音。

examples.en: He left his bag at the hotel.
examples.cn: 他把包落在了旅馆。

examples.en: They bagged the best seats by arriving early.
examples.cn: 他们早到占到了最好的座位。

dict_mnemonic.text: bag 读来短促：布袋一鼓，东西就都收进去了，包也叫 bag。

root: 可能源自古诺斯语 baggi「包裹、一捆」，经中古英语 bagge「袋子」进入英语；由软质容器引申为旅行包，再产生「占得」的口语动词义。

sensesIntro.en: A soft container, a traveller's bag and the act of claiming all begin with putting things inside.
sensesIntro.cn: 软容器、旅行包与占有的动作，都从「把东西装进去」开始。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cloth bag hanging full from a chair.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只鼓鼓的布袋挂在椅背上。

definition_en: to cook food in an oven with dry heat, or to become cooked this way
core_image: 烤箱里一盘面包慢慢鼓起来
scene: 厨房里飘出黄油的香味。She likes to bake bread on Sunday mornings.
sceneCN: 这里 bake 是「烘烤」（第 1 个义项：用烤箱的干热把食物烤熟）；句意是她喜欢在周日早上烤面包。

derivatives.zh: 由 bake 加 -er 构成，义为「面包师；烘焙者」
由 baker 加 -y 构成，义为「面包店」
由 bake 加 -ing 构成，义为「烘焙」

senses.title: To cook in an oven
senses.definition: to cook food with dry heat in an oven
senses.definitionCN: 用烤箱的干热把食物烤熟
senses.example: She likes to bake bread on Sunday mornings.
senses.exampleCN: 她喜欢在周日早上烤面包。
senses.why: Bake is an old English word that has always meant cooking with dry heat rather than over a flame.
senses.whyCN: bake 是古英语词，一直表示用干热而非明火来烹饪。

senses.title: To become cooked
senses.definition: to become cooked or hardened by heat
senses.definitionCN: 因受热而被烤熟或变硬
senses.example: The clay pots were left to bake in the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 那些陶罐被放在太阳下晒硬。
senses.why: If you can bake a thing, the thing itself can bake, which gave the word an intransitive sense.
senses.whyCN: 既然你能烤一样东西，这东西自己也会被烤，于是这个词有了不及物用法。

intro.en: Bake is one of the oldest cooking words in English.
intro.cn: bake 是英语里最古老的烹饪词之一。

items.en: bacan meant 'to cook by dry heat'.
items.cn: bacan 意为「用干热烹制」。

items.en: the word kept its oven sense.
items.cn: 这个词保留了「用烤箱」的含义。

items.en: bake covered bread, pies and pottery.
items.cn: bake 涵盖面包、馅饼与陶器。

items.en: freshly baked became a common phrase.
items.cn: freshly baked 成为常见搭配。

items.en: bake also appears in recipes and oven names.
items.cn: 如今 bake 也出现在食谱与烤箱名称中。

note.en: The look-alike group differs in the first or last sound; the near-meaning group gives other ways of cooking.
note.cn: 形近组在首音或尾音上不同；近义组是其他烹饪方式。

normal.en: The past tense and past participle are both baked.

normal.en: A shop that sells baked goods is a bakery.
normal.cn: 卖烘焙食品的店是 bakery。

normal.en: Bake bread, but boil rice.

normal.en: The vowel is long: bayk.
normal.cn: 元音是长音。

sensesIntro.cn: 在烤箱里烤食物，与食物受热被烤熟，是同一个动词的两面。

definition_en: a steady state, the money left in an account, or to keep something steady
core_image: 天平两端各放一只砝码，指针缓缓停住
scene: 收银台前，店员抬头看了看屏幕。Please check the balance on your card.
sceneCN: 这里 balance 是「余额」（第 2 个义项：账户里剩下的钱）；句意是请查看你卡里的余额。

derivatives.zh: 由 balance 加 -ed 构成，义为「均衡的；平稳的」
由 im- 加 balance 构成，义为「失衡」
由 balance 加 -ing 构成，义为「平衡；权衡」

senses.title: Steady position
senses.definition: a state in which weight is evenly spread and nothing falls
senses.definitionCN: 重量均匀分布、不会倒下的状态
senses.example: She kept her balance on the icy path.
senses.exampleCN: 她在结冰的小路上保持着平衡。
senses.why: Balance came from Latin bilanx, 'two scales', so its first sense is the equal weighing of two sides.
senses.whyCN: balance 来自拉丁语 bilanx「两架天平」，所以最初的义项是两边等重。

senses.title: Money left
senses.definition: the amount of money remaining in an account
senses.definitionCN: 账户中剩余的钱数
senses.example: Please check the balance on your card.
senses.exampleCN: 请查看你卡里的余额。

normal.en: Keep your balance is a common phrase.

normal.en: A bank balance is the money you have left.

sensesIntro.en: Equal weight, money left over and fair judgement are three results of keeping two sides even.

definition_en: a round object used in games, a round mass, or a formal dance
core_image: 草地上一只圆球停在白线边
scene: 操场上孩子们追着跑。He threw the ball across the field.
sceneCN: 这里 ball 是「球」（第 1 个义项：游戏中使用的圆形物体）；句意是他把球扔过场地。

derivatives.zh: 同源词，由意大利语「大球」而来，义为「气球」
由 ball 与 room 构成，义为「舞厅」
由 ball 与 point 构成，义为「圆珠笔」

senses.title: A round object for games
senses.definition: a round object that is thrown, kicked or hit in games
senses.definitionCN: 在游戏中用来投、踢或击打的圆形物体
senses.example: He threw the ball across the field.
senses.exampleCN: 他把球扔过场地。
senses.why: Ball came from Old Norse bollr, a round object, and sport is where the word is used most.
senses.whyCN: ball 来自古诺斯语 bollr「圆形物体」，体育是这个词最常用的领域。

senses.title: A round mass
senses.definition: something gathered into a round shape
senses.definitionCN: 聚成圆球形的一团东西
senses.example: She wound the wool into a tight ball.
senses.exampleCN: 她把毛线绕成紧实的一团。
senses.why: Anything wound or pressed into a round shape looks like a ball, so the word covers balls of wool and snow.
senses.whyCN: 任何被绕成或压成圆形的东西都像球，所以毛线团、雪球也用 ball。

senses.title: A formal dance
senses.definition: a formal social event with dancing
senses.definitionCN: 以跳舞为主的正式社交活动
senses.example: They danced all night at the ball.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在舞会上跳了一整夜。
senses.why: The dance sense came from French bal, a ballroom event, and is now kept mainly for formal occasions.
senses.whyCN: 「舞会」义来自法语的 bal，指在舞厅举行的活动，如今多用于正式场合。

intro.en: Ball came from the Norse word for a round object.
intro.cn: ball 来自诺斯语中表示「圆形物体」的词。

items.en: bal named a round toy or object.

items.cn: ball 涵盖球类游戏与圆团。

items.cn: ball 也指正式的舞会。

items.en: ball is basic in sport and idiom.
items.cn: 如今 ball 是体育与习语中的基本词。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one vowel; the near-meaning group gives round shapes and the dance.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个元音；近义组是圆形物与舞会的说法。

entries.definition: a round model of the earth
a social event with music and dancing

normalIntro.en: A ball is round, bounces and is used in play.

normal.en: The plural is balls.

normal.en: A ball of string is a round mass.

normal.en: A formal dance is also a ball.
normal.cn: 正式舞会也叫 ball。

normal.en: Play ball is a common phrase.
normal.cn: play ball 是常见说法。

normal.en: Keep your eye on the ball means stay focused.
normal.cn: 「keep your eye on the ball」意为保持专注。

abstract.en: See a round ball resting on grass.
abstract.cn: 想象草地上停着一只圆球。

abstract.en: See a ball bouncing off a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象球从墙上弹回。

abstract.en: See a ball of wool on a table.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上的一团毛线。

examples.en: He threw the ball across the field.
examples.cn: 他把球扔过场地。

examples.en: They danced all night at the ball.
examples.cn: 他们在舞会上跳了一整夜。

dict_mnemonic.text: ball 的读音圆滚滚：一只球滚过草地，滚成一团，也滚进舞会。

root: 源自古诺斯语 bollr「圆形物体」，经中古英语 bal 进入英语；由球类用具引申为任何圆团，又借法语 bal 表示正式舞会。

sensesIntro.en: A toy, a round mass and a night of dancing all keep the idea of something round and gathered.
sensesIntro.cn: 玩具、圆团与跳舞的夜晚，都保留了「圆而成团」的意思。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round ball resting on grass.
core.cn: 核心意象：草地上停着一只圆球。

intro.en: Ball joins room and point to make ballroom and ballpoint.
intro.cn: ball 与 room、point 组合，构成 ballroom 与 ballpoint。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base; the word came from Old Norse.

items.meaning: a pen with a rolling ball
a round model of the earth

definition_en: to officially forbid something, or an official order that forbids it
core_image: 门口立起一块写有禁止字样的木牌
scene: 公告贴在体育馆门口。The city decided to ban smoking in parks.
sceneCN: 这里 ban 是「禁止」（第 1 个义项：官方明令不许做某事）；句意是市里决定禁止在公园吸烟。

derivatives.zh: 由 ban 加 -ned 构成，义为「被禁止的」
由 ban 加 -ning 构成，义为「禁止的行为」
同源词，来自古法语 banir，义为「放逐」

senses.title: To forbid officially
senses.definition: to officially say that something must not be done
senses.definitionCN: 官方宣布某事不许做
senses.example: The city decided to ban smoking in parks.
senses.exampleCN: 市里决定禁止在公园吸烟。
senses.why: Ban began as a word for a public proclamation, and an order that forbids something is the modern use.
senses.whyCN: ban 起初指公开宣告，而宣布禁止某事就是它如今的用法。

senses.title: An official order
senses.definition: an official rule that forbids something
senses.definitionCN: 官方禁止某事的规则
senses.example: The government lifted the ban on travel.
senses.exampleCN: 政府解除了旅行禁令。
senses.why: The noun names the proclamation itself, so a ban is the written or announced order.
senses.whyCN: 名词指的是宣告本身，所以 ban 就是那份明令。

intro.en: Ban is an old word for a public proclamation.
intro.cn: ban 是表示「公开宣告」的古词。

items.en: bannan meant 'to summon or proclaim'.

items.en: bannum meant 'a proclamation'.

items.en: ban meant 'a public order'.

items.en: ban narrowed to an official prohibition.

normal.en: Impose a ban means start it.

normal.en: The noun and the verb look the same.

abstract.en: See a hand raised to stop a crowd.

abstract.en: See a red cross over a cigarette.

examples.en: They banned the sale of the old machines.
examples.cn: 他们禁止销售那些旧机器。

root: 源自古英语 bannan「召集、宣告」，与中世纪拉丁语 bannum「公告」同源；由公开宣告缩小为官方的禁止，名词即「禁令」。

sensesIntro.en: The act of forbidding and the order itself are one word in two roles.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden sign at a gate.

latinIntro.cn: 这个词是英语本族词，与中世纪拉丁语 bannum 有亲缘关系。

definition_en: a group of musicians, a thin strip, or a group of people
core_image: 手腕上一根细橡皮带勒出浅痕
scene: 巷口的排练房传出鼓声。The band played three songs before the rain came.
sceneCN: 这里 band 是「乐队」（第 1 个义项：一起演奏音乐的一组人）；句意是乐队在雨来之前演奏了三首歌。

derivatives.zh: 同源词，由 band 加 -age 构成，义为「绷带」
由 band 加 -ed 构成，义为「有条纹的」
由 band 加 -ing 构成，义为「条带分布」

senses.title: A group of musicians
senses.definition: a group of people who play music together
senses.definitionCN: 一起演奏音乐的一群人
senses.example: The band played three songs before the rain came.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队在雨来之前演奏了三首歌。
senses.why: A band first meant a group bound together, and musicians who play as one unit took the name.
senses.whyCN: band 最初指被系在一起的一群人，作为一个整体演奏的乐手就用了这个称呼。

senses.title: A thin strip
senses.definition: a thin flat strip of material that ties or circles something
senses.definitionCN: 用来捆扎或环绕的细长扁条
senses.example: She tied the letters with a rubber band.
senses.exampleCN: 她用橡皮筋把信件捆好。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a strip that binds, from Old French bande, and this is the source of bandage.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是用于捆扎的带子，来自古法语 bande，也是 bandage 的来源。

senses.title: A group of people
senses.definition: a small group of people with a shared purpose
senses.definitionCN: 有共同目的的一小群人
senses.example: A band of travellers stopped at the inn.
senses.exampleCN: 一伙旅人在客栈停下。
senses.why: People bound by a common aim form a band, the same idea of tying that gives the musical group.
senses.whyCN: 因共同目标而系在一起的人就构成一伙，这和乐队的「系在一起」是同一个思路。

definition_en: a sudden loud noise, a hard hit, or hair cut straight across the forehead
core_image: 门被风一吹，砰地撞上门框
scene: 楼道里的窗户没关。The door closed with a loud bang.

senses.title: A sudden loud noise
senses.definition: a short, very loud noise like a gun or a slammed door
senses.definitionCN: 像枪响或关门那样短促而巨大的声音
senses.example: The door closed with a loud bang.
senses.exampleCN: 门砰的一声关上了。
senses.why: Bang is an imitative word, shaped to sound like the noise it names.
senses.whyCN: bang 是拟声词，读音就是模仿它所指的声音。

senses.title: A hard hit
senses.definition: to hit something hard or to close it noisily
senses.definitionCN: 用力击打某物或把它砰地关上
senses.example: He banged the box on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 他把箱子砰地砸在地上。
senses.why: A loud impact makes a bang, so the verb came to mean hitting something with force.
senses.whyCN: 巨大的撞击会发出砰声，所以动词就表示用力撞击。

senses.title: Hair over the forehead
senses.definition: hair cut straight across the forehead
senses.definitionCN: 齐齐剪在额头前的头发
senses.example: She cut her bangs short before the trip.
senses.exampleCN: 出行前她把刘海剪短了。
senses.why: This sense probably comes from the idea of a cut edge, and it is mainly American English.

senses.title: A place for money

definition_en: the act of washing the body in water, or the tub you sit in

scene: 水汽把镜子蒙住了。She took a warm bath after the long walk.

senses.title: Washing in water
senses.definition: the act of washing the whole body in water
senses.definitionCN: 在水中洗净全身的行为
senses.example: She took a warm bath after the long walk.
senses.exampleCN: 长途步行后她洗了个热水澡。
senses.why: Bath comes from Old English baeth, which named both the water and the act of washing in it.
senses.whyCN: bath 来自古英语 baeth，兼指洗澡水与在水中洗浴的行为。

senses.title: The tub
senses.definition: a large container that you fill with water and sit in
senses.definitionCN: 注满水后可以坐进去的大容器
senses.example: The bath was full of hot water.
senses.exampleCN: 浴缸里放满了热水。
senses.why: The container and the act shared one name, so the tub itself can be called a bath.
senses.whyCN: 容器与行为共用一个名称，所以浴缸本身也叫 bath。
